message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"13cf3fa9f6edda47ceeaa2c4c06ad98db5dfba746a4aabef2a1662ed8bb7cffa","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-in-class-std:lineage:45","source_registry_sha256":"2800087d52ca58455ac6dac735a6e1bd60a4442f9e09c2356d96bd9ed8102504","units":[{"unit_id":"sec02-u01","module_id":"sec02-m01","objective_ids":["sec02-u01"],"title":{"text":"How the skills exam is scored","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-R09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing which mistakes only cost points and which end the exam lets you focus practice on the errors that matter most.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F05","sec02-F06"]},{"text":"Retake waits shape your schedule, so a failure close to a deadline can cost more than a week.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"During her skills exam, Nia drives a little slowly and then turns right on red at a corner posted No Turn on Red.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Driving too slowly counts against her, but disobeying a no-turn-on-red sign is an automatic failure.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F03"]},"result":{"text":"Nia fails the exam and must wait seven days before she may retake it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the examiner always stops the exam the moment you fail.","fact_ids":["sec02-R11"]},"correction":{"text":"Even after a driver has failed, the examiner may choose to let the drive continue, so a finished drive does not mean a pass.","fact_ids":["sec02-R11"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Points for slips, failure for signs, speed and center lines.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F05","sec02-F06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver straddles two marked lanes for a block during the skills exam. Does that only cost points?","fact_ids":["sec02-F06"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Straddling marked lanes is an automatic failure.","fact_ids":["sec02-F06"]},"rationale":{"text":"Lane-position failures include crossing a solid yellow line, drifting left of center and straddling marked lanes.","fact_ids":["sec02-F06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"What the examiner watches","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Some errors cost points.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Some errors end the exam.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Failures bring a wait.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on how the driving skills exam is scored. The examiner is watching two kinds of mistakes. Some errors lower your score, and enough of them can fail you. Others are automatic failures that decide the result on their own. Knowing which is which tells you where to focus your practice. You will also learn what happens after a failed exam, including how long you must wait before trying again and why a third failure on a permit carries a much longer wait than the first. Let us start with the scoring.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F03","sec02-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Errors that cost points","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-R09","sec02-R10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wipers, defroster, both hands, right gear.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-R09","sec02-R10"]},{"text":"Too slow, needless stops, rolling past lines.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-R09","sec02-R10"]},{"text":"Reversing and signal habits.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-R09","sec02-R10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Several everyday errors can lower your score or fail you. They include not using the defroster or wipers when needed, not keeping both hands on the wheel, picking the wrong gear and not signaling. Driving too slowly, stopping when there is no need, rolling past a crosswalk, stop line or stop sign, turning into or out of the wrong lane and skipping the blind-spot check also count against you. Reversing is scored too, including backing out of a parking space. Slowing while changing lanes, reversing too fast, leaving the signal on and following parked vehicles too closely can also cost points.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-R09","sec02-R10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Signs, curbs and seat belts","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ignoring a sign or signal fails.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04"]},{"text":"Backing over a curb fails.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04"]},{"text":"No seat belt fails.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Now the automatic failures. Disobeying a yield sign, a stop sign, a school zone sign or a no-turn-on-red sign, or disobeying a traffic signal, fails the exam on the spot. So does backing over a curb or striking a parked vehicle. Two more are easy to overlook because they are not about steering at all. Not following the examiner's instructions is an automatic failure, and so is not using your seat belt. Before you even start the engine, buckle up, listen carefully to each instruction, and treat every sign and signal on the route as a pass or fail moment.","fact_ids":["sec02-F03","sec02-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Speed, lanes and other users","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Speeding or too fast for conditions.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},{"text":"Solid yellow, left of center, straddling lanes.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},{"text":"Yield, emergency vehicles, buses, crashes.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"More automatic failures involve speed and position. Speeding, driving too fast for the conditions, not reacting to hazardous conditions and using the wrong lane all fail the exam. Passing in a no-passing zone or otherwise going over a solid yellow line, drifting left of the street center and straddling marked lanes fail it too. Finally, other road users. Getting too close to pedestrians or bicycles, not pulling over and stopping for emergency vehicles or school buses, causing a crash, failing to yield and breaking railroad crossing laws are all automatic failures.","fact_ids":["sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"After a failed exam","fact_ids":["sec02-R11","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Examiner may let the drive continue.","fact_ids":["sec02-R11","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R01"]},{"text":"Wait seven days to retake.","fact_ids":["sec02-R11","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R01"]},{"text":"Third failure on a permit: two months.","fact_ids":["sec02-R11","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"A failure does not always end the drive. The BMV examiner may choose to let the drive continue even after you have failed, so finishing the route is not proof of a pass. If you fail, you must wait seven days before you may retake the skills exam. There is a stricter rule for repeated failures. A permit holder who fails the skills exam a third time must wait two months from that last failure before testing again. Keep those two numbers apart: seven days for an ordinary retake, and two months after a third failure while still on a permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-R11","sec02-F08","sec02-F09","sec02-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Mixing up the waits","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: two months after any failure.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},{"text":"Seven days unless it is the third failure.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Students hear about the two-month wait and assume it applies to every failed skills exam. It does not. After an ordinary failure, the wait is seven days. Only a permit holder who fails for the third time faces the two-month wait, counted from that latest failed attempt. A second trap is the knowledge exam. Its retake rule is the next business day, which is a different exam with a different wait. When a question asks about a retake, first decide which exam it is, then whether this is the third skills failure on a permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a lane mistake","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Straddling two lanes.","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-F02"]},{"text":"Points or failure?","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: during the skills exam a driver straddles two marked lanes for most of a block. Does that only cost points, or is it an automatic failure? Think about the lane-position list. Passing in a no-passing zone, crossing a solid yellow line, drifting left of the street center and straddling marked lanes are each automatic failures. So the answer is that it fails the exam. Compare that with turning into the wrong lane at a corner, which appears among the errors that count against you. If you said points only, review the lane-position failures.","fact_ids":["sec02-F06","sec02-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Scoring in one view","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slips cost points.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},{"text":"Signs, speed, lanes, yielding fail.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},{"text":"Seven days or two months.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. Control slips such as forgetting the wipers, one hand on the wheel, the wrong gear, missing signals, rolling stops and skipped blind-spot checks cost points, and reversing is scored. Automatic failures include ignoring signs or signals, backing over a curb, hitting a parked car, ignoring instructions, no seat belt, speeding, crossing a solid yellow line, straddling lanes, crowding pedestrians, not yielding or stopping for emergency vehicles and school buses, crashes and railroad violations. After a failure wait seven days, or two months after a third failure on a permit.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-F02","sec02-F03","sec02-F04","sec02-F05","sec02-F06","sec02-F07","sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u02","module_id":"sec02-m02","objective_ids":["sec02-u02"],"title":{"text":"Financial liability for minors","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A minor cannot get a permit or probationary license until an adult accepts financial responsibility for the minor's driving.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F12"]},{"text":"The signer can withdraw at any time, which cancels the minor's credential, so the arrangement matters for as long as the teen drives.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13"]},{"text":"Minors in Department of Child Services care follow a different route and show qualifying insurance instead of an adult signature.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Owen, seventeen, lives with his mother after his parents divorced, and both parents are willing to sign for him.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},"reasoning":{"text":"The legal order puts the custodial parent or that parent's designee first, ahead of the noncustodial parent.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11"]},"result":{"text":"Owen's mother appears at the branch, shows valid identification and signs, becoming jointly responsible with Owen for damage he causes.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F12"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a withdrawn financial liability signature leaves the teen's license in place until renewal.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13"]},"correction":{"text":"The signer's written withdrawal on the state form cancels the minor's permit or license, and the minor needs an amended permit with a different signer.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-R12"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Someone signs, someone shares, and withdrawing cancels.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A minor in the care and supervision of the Department of Child Services has no adult to sign. What must the minor show instead?","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"answer":{"text":"A motor vehicle insurance policy that meets Indiana's minimum liability standards.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14"]},"rationale":{"text":"Minors in DCS care need no adult signature but must show a qualifying insurance policy.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F10"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Who answers for a minor","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"An adult signs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"The adult shares responsibility.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on financial liability for minors. When someone under eighteen applies for a learner's permit or a probationary license, an adult must step forward and accept responsibility for the minor's driving. This lesson explains who must sign, the legal order for choosing that adult, what the signature means, and what happens if the adult later changes their mind. You will also see the special rule for minors in the care of the Department of Child Services, who follow a different path because there may be no parent available to sign.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who signs, and in what order","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Adult appears at a branch and signs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},{"text":"Custodial parent first, then noncustodial.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},{"text":"Then guardian, then any willing adult.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"A permit or probationary license applicant under eighteen needs an adult to appear at a BMV branch and sign a sworn or affirmed financial liability statement. The signer is chosen in a legal order. First comes the custodial parent or that parent's designee. Next is the noncustodial parent or that parent's designee. After that comes the custodial guardian, and finally any other willing adult. The order matters when more than one adult could sign. Work down the list from the top, and the first available adult in that order is the one who signs for the minor.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"What signing means","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Joint and several responsibility for damage.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Withdraw any time with the state form.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"DCS minors show insurance instead.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"The adult who signs becomes jointly and severally responsible with the minor for damage caused by the minor's driving, and must show valid identification from the BMV identity document list. That is a real legal commitment, and it can be ended. The signer can withdraw at any time with State Form fifty-five eight thirty-four, and that written request cancels the minor's permit or license. The minor must then apply for an amended learner's permit with a different adult signing. A minor in the care and supervision of the Department of Child Services needs no adult signature but must show an insurance policy meeting Indiana's minimum liability standards.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The withdrawal trap","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: the license survives a withdrawal.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F10"]},{"text":"Withdrawal cancels it.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some families think that once a teen has a license, the adult's signature no longer matters. In fact, the signer can withdraw at any time, and the written request on the state form cancels the minor's permit or license right away, not at the next renewal. The teen cannot simply sign for themselves either. To keep learning, the minor must apply for an amended learner's permit with a different adult signing for financial liability. So the signature is not a one-time formality; it is the foundation the minor's credential rests on while the minor is under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the DCS route","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Minor in DCS care.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},{"text":"No adult to sign.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},{"text":"What is shown instead?","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a sixteen-year-old in the care and supervision of the Department of Child Services applies for a learner's permit, and there is no adult available to sign. What must the minor show instead of a financial liability signature? Recall the DCS rule. Such a minor needs no adult signature, but must show a motor vehicle insurance policy that meets Indiana's minimum liability standards. So the answer is a qualifying insurance policy. Every other minor follows the signing order that starts with the custodial parent. If you said a caseworker signs, review this exception.","fact_ids":["sec02-F14","sec02-F10","sec02-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Liability in brief","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"An adult signs in a set order.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Signer shares responsibility.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},{"text":"Withdrawal cancels the credential.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us wrap up. Every permit or probationary license applicant under eighteen needs an adult to appear at a branch and sign a financial liability statement. The signer comes from a legal order: custodial parent or designee, noncustodial parent or designee, custodial guardian, then any other willing adult. The signer shows valid identification and becomes jointly and severally responsible with the minor for driving damage. A withdrawal on the state form cancels the credential, and the minor then needs an amended permit with a new signer, while minors in DCS care show qualifying insurance instead.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F11","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-R12","sec02-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u03","module_id":"sec02-m03","objective_ids":["sec02-u03"],"title":{"text":"Meeting the license requirements","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F17","sec02-F18"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A license application fails if any one requirement is missing, so knowing the full checklist saves a wasted visit.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18"]},{"text":"Age, permit time and practice hours each have fixed numbers that apply to you depending on your situation.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Lena is sixteen years and two hundred days old, did not take a BMV licensed driver education program, and has held her permit for two hundred days with fifty logged hours.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F27"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Without driver education, the minimum license age is sixteen years and two hundred seventy days, so the age rule is not yet met even though her permit time and hours are.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Lena must wait until she reaches sixteen years and two hundred seventy days before applying.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19","sec02-R02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking that a daytime-only restriction G cuts the practice requirement below fifty hours.","fact_ids":["sec02-F22"]},"correction":{"text":"Restriction G removes only the night-hour part; the full fifty hours are still required.","fact_ids":["sec02-F22","sec02-F21"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Sixteen with class, one-eighty on the permit, fifty hours with ten at night.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F20","sec02-F22"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Kai is twenty-two and wants a license. Does he need logged supervised practice hours?","fact_ids":["sec02-F21"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes. An applicant eighteen or older must log at least fifty supervised hours.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21"]},"rationale":{"text":"The fifty-hour rule covers adults too, with a supervisor aged twenty-five or more or a licensed spouse aged twenty-one or more.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-F27"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your license checklist","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21"]},"lines":[{"text":"Age, permit time, practice hours.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21"]},{"text":"Proofs and three exams.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21"]}],"narration":{"text":"Welcome to the lesson on meeting the license requirements. Getting a driver's license is a checklist, and every box must be ticked. You must reach the minimum age, hold your learner's permit long enough, log your supervised practice, prove who you are, and pass three exams. Each requirement has its own number, and those numbers change depending on whether you took driver education, how old you are and whether you are applying with a disability. By the end of this lesson you will be able to look at an applicant and say whether they are ready to apply.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F19","sec02-F20","sec02-F21"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The checklist and the ages","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-R02","sec02-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Under twenty-one: probationary license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-R02","sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Knowledge exam before skills exam.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-R02","sec02-F15"]},{"text":"Sixteen with driver education.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-R02","sec02-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"To get a license you must meet the age rule, hold a valid Indiana permit for the required time unless you hold an unexpired license from another jurisdiction, prove identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency, and pass vision, knowledge and skills exams. The knowledge exam must be completed before the skills exam, which is taken with a BMV examiner or an approved driver training school. The minimum age is sixteen if you completed a BMV licensed driver education program, and sixteen years and two hundred seventy days if you did not. Any license issued to someone under twenty-one is a probationary license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18","sec02-F19","sec02-R02","sec02-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Permit time and practice hours","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-F27","sec02-F21","sec02-F22"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hold the permit one hundred eighty days.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-F27","sec02-F21","sec02-F22"]},{"text":"Fifty supervised hours.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-F27","sec02-F21","sec02-F22"]},{"text":"Ten of them at night.","fact_ids":["sec02-F20","sec02-F27","sec02-F21","sec02-F22"]}],"narration":{"text":"You must have held a valid Indiana learner's permit for at least one hundred eighty days. The only exception is an applicant eighteen or older with a documented disability who has finished rehabilitation training with a BMV-recognized specialist. Practice hours are required at every age. An applicant under eighteen seeking a probationary license must complete at least fifty hours of supervised practice, and an applicant eighteen or older must log at least fifty hours too. You may use several logs, and if you are under eighteen a parent or legal guardian signs them. Who you practice with matters.
